topics.content:
**Computer:** An electronic machine that accepts data, processes it and gives out information.

**Main parts:**
- **Input devices:** keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone.
- **Processing unit:** the CPU, which carries out instructions.
- **Output devices:** monitor, printer, speaker.
- **Storage devices:** hard disk, flash drive, memory card.

**Hardware and software:** Hardware is the physical part you can touch. Software is the set of instructions that tells the computer what to do.

**Uses of computers:** typing documents, calculations, drawing, communication, learning and entertainment.

**Care of the computer:** Keep it away from water and dust, use a stabiliser, shut down properly, and do not eat near the keyboard.

**Word processing** means using a computer program to type, edit and print text.

**Examples:** Microsoft Word, Google Docs and WPS Writer.

**Things you can do:**
- Type and correct text
- Change font, size and colour
- Make text bold, italic or underlined
- Align text left, centre, right or justify
- Add tables and pictures
- Check spelling
- Save and print

**Saving work:** Click File → Save, choose a folder and give the document a clear name.

**Useful shortcuts:** Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+Z undo.

**Good habits:** Sit upright, keep the keyboard clean, save often and proofread before printing.

**Internet:** A network that connects computers all over the world so they can share information.

**Things you can do online:** search for information, send messages, attend online classes, watch educational videos and buy or sell goods.

**Browser:** Software used to open websites, such as Chrome, Firefox or Edge.

**Search engine:** A website that helps you find information, such as Google or Bing.

**Email:** A message sent electronically from one person to another.

**Email address example:** student@example.com — the part before @ is the username, and the part after @ is the domain.

**Email parts:** To, Subject, Message and Attachment.

**Online safety:** Never share your password, do not open strange links, and tell a trusted adult if something online makes you uncomfortable.

**Spreadsheet:** A program that keeps data in rows and columns and can calculate totals and averages.

**Examples:** Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets.

**Cell:** The box where a row and a column meet, such as A1.

**Rows and columns:** Rows are horizontal and numbered; columns are vertical and lettered.

**Simple formulas:**
- =SUM(A1:A5) adds the numbers
- =AVERAGE(A1:A5) finds the average
- =MAX(A1:A5) finds the largest
- =MIN(A1:A5) finds the smallest

**Every formula begins with =**

**Uses:** keeping a class mark list, calculating totals in a shop, and drawing simple charts.

**Good practice:** Label your columns, check your formula range and save your work regularly.
